standard_prerequisites.name: Structure and variable assignment
standard_prerequisites.statement: A first-order structure fixes a domain together with interpretations of the constant, relation and function symbols; a variable assignment maps variables into the domain.
standard_prerequisites.use: The two structures and the shared assignment are the setting of the statement (source lines 883-888).

standard_prerequisites.name: Value of a term and satisfaction of a formula
standard_prerequisites.statement: The value of a term in a structure under an assignment, and the satisfaction relation between a structure, a formula and an assignment, both defined by recursion on the syntax.
standard_prerequisites.use: The two inductions follow exactly these recursions (source lines 894-899).

core_obligations: Prove the term claim: by induction on the term t, show that the value of t in the first structure under s equals its value in the second structure under s, using that the two structures agree on the constants and function symbols occurring in t (source lines 894-895).

Prove the formula claim: by induction on the formula A, show that A is satisfied in the first structure under s exactly when it is satisfied in the second, using the term claim for the atomic case and the induction hypothesis in the propositional and quantifier cases (source lines 895-899).

proof_roadmap.step: Induction on terms: the values of a term agree in the two structures.
Induction on formulas: satisfaction agrees, with the atomic case supplied by the term claim.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own proposition prop:extensionality at source lines 883-892: for a formula A and two structures whose domains and whose interpretations of every constant, relation symbol and function symbol occurring in A coincide, satisfaction of A under any assignment is the same in the two structures. The proof at source lines 894-899 is short but it is an induction specification rather than a one-line appeal: it prescribes first proving by induction on terms that the value of every term is the same in the two structures, and then proving the proposition by induction on the formula, using the term claim as the induction basis, that is, in the atomic case. The content is the choice of the two nested inductions and the recognition that the hypothesis must quantify only over the symbols occurring in the formula, since symbols outside it may be interpreted differently. The statement records the hypothesis but not the induction structure the proof asks for. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
